title: Sell Mineral Rights in Newport, OH
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Newport, OH | Washington County
metaDescription: Newport sits on the Ohio River in Washington County's Utica flank. See how this small river community's mineral rights typically get evaluated.
heroLead: Newport is a small unincorporated community on the Ohio River in Washington County, in a region with one of the longest oil and gas production histories in the country, layered underneath the current Utica/Point Pleasant flank position.
intro: Washington County's oil history stretches back to the 1800s, and river communities like Newport have seen more than one wave of leasing and drilling over the decades. For a mineral owner here, the practical challenge is usually untangling which of those historical leases, if any, are still active, rather than figuring out whether the area has ever had oil and gas activity at all.

sections.heading: Layered leasing history along the river
paragraphs: It's common for river-corridor tracts near Newport to have multiple historical lease filings on record, some going back generations, most of them expired but not necessarily cleared from the title record. Sorting through which leases are actually still in force takes real research, not a quick glance.

sections.heading: Washington County's flank position today
paragraphs: Modern Utica/Point Pleasant activity has generally been lighter in Washington County than in core counties like Belmont or Monroe further north and east. Newport-area land is valued with that context in mind, alongside whatever older shallow production history the tract may carry.

sections.heading: Recorder records in Marietta
paragraphs: The Washington County Recorder's office in Marietta holds the deed and lease history for Newport. Given the depth of this area's oil and gas past, plan on a thorough title search rather than a cursory one before moving forward with a sale.

faqs.question: Why does Newport have so much old lease paperwork?
faqs.answer: Washington County has one of the longest oil and gas production histories in the country, dating to the 1800s, and river communities like Newport have seen multiple leasing waves over the decades.

faqs.question: Is Newport in the current Utica core?
faqs.answer: No, it's generally in the flank position. The thicker core runs through counties further north and east, like Belmont and Monroe.

faqs.question: How do I find out which of the old leases on my land are still active?
faqs.answer: A title search at the Washington County Recorder's office in Marietta will show the recorded lease history, though determining which are truly still in force may require checking for held-by-production status on any associated wells.

faqs.question: How do I tell if an old lease near Newport is still legally active?
faqs.answer: Check whether a well was ever drilled on the associated unit and whether it's still producing in paying quantities. Without production, most older leases in this area have lapsed by now.
